title: Use It Twice
goal: Make both print statements work — without any cloning.
hints: Does print_name need to OWN the name, or just look at it?
A &String parameter works, but there is a more flexible type that accepts both &String and string literals.
explanation: Passing `name` moves the String into print_name, so the later `println!("{name}")` uses a moved value. Cloning works but pays an allocation for nothing. Borrowing with `&name` lets main keep ownership. For the parameter, `&str` beats `&String`: deref coercion means a `&String` argument converts automatically, and the function also accepts literals and slices — Clippy's ptr_arg lint flags `&String` for exactly this reason.
